Verified 2026-09-05 by running `npm run viewports` (local, port 3301) and
`npm run viewports:live` (https://www.coframe.com) back to back and diffing

why: At 1024x1366 @2x the live coframe.com page itself overflows horizontally by
27px, and the replica reproduces it exactly rather than diverging.
Measured, local vs live, from scrape/viewport-report.json:
tooWide[0]    div.cursor-container w=1051 right=1051  (identical both sides)
Cause upstream: #cursor-container is the absolutely-positioned overlay that
hosts the animated cursor clones. The site's own script (captured as
script-23.js) sizes it to document scrollWidth, and at this specific
width/dpr the value it latches is 27px wider than the viewport.
Deliberately NOT 'fixed': clamping the overlay would make the replica
diverge from the original page it is supposed to reproduce. Note the replica
reported 0 console errors / 0 failed requests / 0 remote requests at this
viewport, while live reported 2 console errors and 10 failed requests.
